scenes.dialogue: The case began with Civil Services candidates whose parents worked in public sector undertakings. Those posts had no formal equivalence with government posts.
So the Department of Personnel used an income test for them instead. The Tribunal disagreed with that, and three High Courts upheld the Tribunal's view.
On the eleventh of March, the Supreme Court dismissed the government's appeals, rejecting mechanical exclusion on salary income, with six months to comply.

scenes.dialogue: The government then asked that completed selections stay intact, and sought two years to fix equivalence of posts. Candidates called it a bid for a rehearing.
